title: Republic of Indonesia formally proclaimed as unitary state
note: The RIS was dissolved and the unitary Republic proclaimed on 17 August 1950, the fifth anniversary of independence. Year, mechanism, and Sukarno's role all confirmed.

title: West Irian dispute with the Netherlands begins
note: Following the December 1949 Dutch sovereignty transfer, Netherlands retained West New Guinea. Sukarno made recovery a national priority, consistent with sources.

title: Parliamentary democracy experiment begins
note: Indonesia adopted a provisional parliamentary constitution in 1950; cabinet instability and coalition fragmentation are well-documented until Guided Democracy in 1959.

title: Army internal conflict — October 17 Affair
note: Occurred 17 October 1952; soldiers demanded Sukarno dissolve parliament, Nasution removed after parliament reconvened in late November. Year and core facts match.

title: Darul Islam insurgency intensifies in West Java
note: Darul Islam was proclaimed 7 August 1949; guerrilla operations in West Java continued through the 1950s under Kartosuwiryo, captured 1962. Assigning 1952 as intensification year is consistent with the period.

title: First general elections — four parties dominate
note: Held 29 September 1955; PNI, Masyumi, NU and PKI were the big four. Over 37 million voters. No single-party majority. All core facts match.

title: Bandung Asian-African Conference — birth of Non-Alignment
note: 18–24 April 1955, 29 nations attended. Sukarno was key organiser. The Non-Aligned Movement formally founded in 1961 as stated in the event description. All facts confirmed.

title: Sukarno declares Guided Democracy — end of parliamentary era
note: Martial law declared 14 March 1957; Guided Democracy ideology laid out 17 August 1957. The full formalisation came with the 1959 decree. Year 1957 as the declaration is accurate.

title: Nationalization of Dutch assets — 700 companies expropriated
note: Worker seizures began 30 November 1957 and formal nationalization law (No. 86/1958) was issued December 1958. Sources consistently cite 246 companies formally nationalised, not 700; the '700' figure is unconfirmed. Year is plausible as the process started in December 1957.

title: PRRI-Permesta regional rebellions erupt — CIA covert support exposed
note: PRRI proclaimed February 1958; CIA B-26 (actually A-26 Invader) flown by Allen Pope shot down over Ambon 18 May 1958. Exposé confirmed. Minor terminology: type described as 'B-26' matches period reporting.

title: 1945 Constitution restored by presidential decree — Guided Democracy formalized
note: Presidential Decree No. 150 of 5 July 1959 restored the 1945 constitution and dissolved the Constituent Assembly. All core facts confirmed.

title: West Irian military confrontation — Konfrontasi with the Netherlands
note: Indonesia severed ties with Netherlands in August 1960; Trikora decree issued December 1961; Soviet military aid confirmed; New York Agreement 1962. The event year 1960 marks the start of the military phase accurately.

title: New York Agreement transfers West Irian to Indonesia
note: Agreement signed 15 August 1962, mediated by Ellsworth Bunker of the US. UNTEA transferred administration to Indonesia 1 May 1963. All core facts confirmed.

title: Konfrontasi against Malaysia declared
note: Malaysia Federation proclaimed 16 September 1963; Sukarno announced 'Crush Malaysia' on 25 September 1963. Cross-border raids into Sarawak/Sabah confirmed. Year and key facts verified.

title: PKI becomes world's third largest communist party
note: Sources consistently describe PKI as the 'largest non-ruling communist party in the world' (not third largest) by the early 1960s, ahead of non-Soviet/non-Chinese parties. The 'third largest' framing may be using a different ranking. Three-million membership figure confirmed.

title: Hyperinflation and economic collapse under Guided Democracy
note: Inflation was extremely high in 1964–65 (sources cite 600%+ annually); foreign exchange depletion and rice shortages documented. Year and core facts plausible and consistent with the period.

title: September 30th Movement, counter-coup, and anti-communist mass killings
note: G30S on night of 30 Sept–1 Oct 1965; Suharto crushed it within hours; 500,000–1 million estimated deaths Oct 1965–mid-1966. All core facts confirmed.

title: Supersemar — formal transfer of power to Suharto
note: Signed 11 March 1966; MPRS stripped Sukarno of titles March 1967 and appointed Suharto acting president. Indonesia rejoined UN/IMF/World Bank. All facts confirmed.

title: End of Konfrontasi with Malaysia — Jakarta-Kuala Lumpur normalization
note: Peace agreement signed 11 August 1966 in Bangkok (Bangkok Accord). Indonesia joined ASEAN in 1967. All core facts confirmed.

title: ASEAN founded — Indonesia as leading member
note: ASEAN Declaration signed 8 August 1967 in Bangkok by Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand. All facts confirmed.

title: Suharto formally becomes president — New Order begins
note: MPRS removed Sukarno March 1967 and appointed Suharto acting president; formally elected March 1968. Three pillars of New Order (dwifungsi, technocrats, repression) well-documented.

title: Berkeley Mafia economic stabilization program
note: Widjojo Nitisastro, Ali Wardhana, Emil Salim led stabilization from 1966–67; IMF/World Bank/IGGI support confirmed; inflation reduced from 600%+ to double-digits within two years.

title: Act of Free Choice — West Irian controversially integrated as Irian Jaya
note: 1,025 hand-picked delegates voted unanimously in August 1969. UN General Assembly 'took note' without endorsing. Renamed Irian Jaya. All facts confirmed.

title: First New Order general elections — Golkar dominance established
note: Golkar won 62.80 percent in July 1971 elections. Nine parties disadvantaged. Pattern repeated across six Suharto elections. All core facts confirmed.

title: OPEC oil price shock — Indonesia benefits from oil boom
note: 1973 OPEC embargo and oil price quadrupling benefited Indonesia as a significant oil exporter. Oil revenues funded development; later vulnerability when prices collapsed documented. Core facts consistent.

title: Malari riots — anti-Japanese protests in Jakarta
note: 15–16 January 1974; triggered by Japanese PM Tanaka's visit. Japanese cars burned, 11 killed. Suharto arrested critics and tightened press controls. All core facts confirmed.

title: East Timor invaded and annexed — estimated 100,000–180,000 deaths
note: Fretilin declared independence 28 November 1975; Indonesian invasion launched 7 December 1975. Death estimates range 100,000–200,000 over the occupation. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Pertamina crisis — state oil company defaults on $10 billion debt
note: In February 1975 Pertamina disclosed $10 billion+ in debt; government bailout followed; Ibnu Sutowo removed March 1976. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Gerakan Aceh Merdeka (GAM) founded
note: GAM was founded 4 December 1976, not 1977. The event year is off by one year.

title: Petition of 50 challenges Suharto's authority
note: Fifty prominent Indonesians signed the petition in May 1980 accusing Suharto of misusing Pancasila. Blacklisting of signatories confirmed. Year and core facts match.

title: Deforestation accelerates in outer islands
note: Deforestation did accelerate significantly during the Suharto era; military-connected timber concessions are documented. No single 1980 landmark event is identified; this is a multi-year trend presented as an event.

title: Petrus mysterious shootings — extrajudicial killing campaign
note: Petrus shootings started August 1982 (Operasi Clurit); ran through 1985. Suharto acknowledged them in his 1988 biography. Death estimates range up to 8,500 (description says 3,000–5,000, plausible). All core facts confirmed.

title: Oil price collapse forces economic reform and devaluation
note: Oil prices fell sharply from 1982–83; rupiah devalued 38 percent in 1983; banking deregulation followed. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Tanjung Priok massacre
note: Occurred 12 September 1984; military fired on Muslim protesters at Tanjung Priok port. Government count 24 killed; survivor estimates much higher. Minor discrepancy: event says 'between 24 and several hundred' which matches sources.

title: Oil price collapse to $10 — structural adjustment and manufacturing pivot
note: Oil prices collapsed to ~$10/barrel in 1986; Indonesia responded with deregulation and manufacturing push. Japanese/Korean/Taiwanese FDI followed. Year and core facts confirmed.

title: Aceh declared Military Operations Zone (DOM)
note: DOM declared in response to GAM attacks in 1989, with large-scale military operations from early 1990. Wikipedia titles the operation 1990–1998 but DOM designation began in 1989. The event's death toll of 2,000+ is a conservative estimate; sources report 9,000–12,000 killed.

title: Dili massacre in East Timor — filmed and broadcast worldwide
note: 12 November 1991; at least 250 killed at Santa Cruz Cemetery; filmed by Max Stahl and broadcast worldwide. US Congress cut IMET. All core facts confirmed.

title: Tempo, Editor, and DeTik magazines banned
note: Bans issued 21 June 1994 following coverage of German warships purchase controversy (not 'arms purchases' generally, but same trigger). AJI founded in response. All core facts confirmed.

title: PDI headquarters stormed — Megawati ousted in Black July
note: 27 July 1996; police and military forces stormed PDI headquarters; Komnas HAM recorded 5 killed, 149 injured, 23 missing. Description says 'at least five' which matches official count.

title: Asian financial crisis devastates Indonesian economy
note: Thai baht devalued July 1997; rupiah collapsed from ~Rp2,500 to over Rp16,000; IMF $43 billion rescue package confirmed. All core facts verified.

title: May 1998 riots, anti-Chinese violence, and fall of Suharto
note: Trisakti University students killed 12 May 1998 (four, not 'four students' as stated — matches). Suharto resigned 21 May 1998 handing power to Habibie. Estimated 1,000 deaths confirmed. All core facts verified.

title: Reformasi — democratic transition begins
note: Habibie released prisoners, lifted press restrictions, legalised trade unions after Suharto's resignation; transition to multi-party democracy documented. All core facts confirmed.

title: First free elections since 1955 — Wahid elected president
note: June 1999 legislative elections; PDI-P 34%, Golkar 22%; MPR elected Wahid (PKB) as president over Megawati. All core facts confirmed.

title: East Timor independence referendum and post-ballot militia violence
note: Referendum 30 August 1999; 78.5% voted for independence; approximately 1,400 civilians killed post-ballot (description says '1,400 people', some sources say 1,500). Infrastructure destruction and 300,000 displaced confirmed.

title: Big Bang decentralization laws transform governance
note: Laws 22 and 25 of 1999 enacted; devolution to 400+ districts effective 2001. Designed partly to prevent separatism. Core facts confirmed.

title: Sectarian violence in Maluku — over 5,000 killed
note: Violence began January 1999 and escalated through 2000; 5,000 deaths and hundreds of thousands displaced documented. Laskar Jihad infiltration confirmed. Malino II peace accord in 2002 confirmed.

title: Bali bombings — 202 killed in Indonesia's deadliest terrorist attack
note: 12 October 2002; 202 killed including 88 Australians; Jemaah Islamiyah confirmed responsible. All core facts verified.

title: Aceh martial law and major military offensive
note: Megawati declared martial law in Aceh May 2003; 40,000 troops deployed; GAM fighters and civilians killed. Tsunami-enabled peace eventually followed. All core facts confirmed.

title: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami — 167,000 Indonesians killed
note: 26 December 2004; magnitude 9.1–9.3; 167,540 dead or missing in Indonesia alone. $7 billion international reconstruction pledges confirmed. All core facts verified.

title: First direct presidential election — Yudhoyono elected
note: First direct presidential election held July–September 2004; SBY won runoff with 60.62% (event says 61%, minor rounding). All core facts confirmed.

title: Helsinki peace agreement ends Aceh conflict
note: MoU signed 15 August 2005; mediated by Martti Ahtisaari (former Finnish president, not just 'Finnish president'). 29-year conflict referenced. GAM disarmed and abandoned independence claim. All facts confirmed.

title: Lapindo mudflow disaster in East Java
note: Began 29 May 2006; Sidoarjo, East Java; Lapindo Brantas (Bakrie family) linked. Displaced 13,000 families (event says 40,000 people — discrepancy, but 13,000 families could be ~40,000–65,000 people). Core facts confirmed.

title: Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) gains momentum
note: KPK established 2004; gained significant momentum with high-profile convictions from 2007–2008; faced persistent attempts to weaken it. All core facts confirmed.

title: Global financial crisis — Indonesia maintains positive growth
note: Indonesia grew 4.5% in 2009 — one of very few major economies with positive growth alongside China and India. Rupiah and stock market impacts confirmed. G20 membership confirmed. All core facts verified.

title: Yudhoyono re-elected with absolute first-round majority
note: SBY won July 2009 with 60.8% — first president to win first-round outright majority. Infrastructure investment and CCT programmes confirmed in second term. All facts verified.

title: Commodity supercycle — Indonesia becomes world's largest coal and palm oil exporter
note: Indonesia was the world's largest thermal coal exporter and largest palm oil exporter by around 2011; export revenue figures ($28B coal, $17B palm oil) are consistent with the period. Core facts plausible and well-documented.

title: Jokowi wins presidential election — outsider defeats establishment
note: Jokowi won 53.15% on 9 July 2014, defeating Prabowo. Prabowo initially refused to accept result. Event describes 53%, confirmed.

title: Fuel subsidy elimination — infrastructure pivot
note: Jokowi eliminated gasoline and diesel subsidies in late 2014; freed funds redirected to infrastructure. $15–20B annually freed is consistent with reported figures. Core facts confirmed.

title: Haze crisis from peat and forest fires
note: Severe peat/forest fires 2015; ~2.6 million hectares burned; transboundary haze to Malaysia/Singapore/Thailand confirmed. Carbon emissions exceeded EU28 daily average. All core facts verified.

title: Ahok blasphemy case and Islamist mass mobilizations
note: Ahok blasphemy accusation, 'Action 212' rally at Monas confirmed (estimated 500,000+), two-year conviction confirmed. All core facts verified.

title: Nickel ore export ban — downstream industrialization strategy
note: The nickel ore export ban was first imposed in 2014 (then partially lifted), reinstated from January 2020; the 2017 date in the event appears to reference the announcement or re-activation period. The framing is generally accurate but the precise 2017 anchoring of the ban is not the canonical date (2020 is the clearest enforcement date). Insufficient source found to confirm 2017 as the key announcement year for this specific policy.

title: Lombok and Palu earthquakes — series of catastrophic disasters
note: Lombok earthquakes August 2018 (550+ deaths); Palu earthquake 28 September 2018 (7.5 magnitude, 4,340 deaths, soil liquefaction). All core facts confirmed.

title: Jokowi re-elected — Prabowo defeated again; new capital Nusantara announced
note: Jokowi won April 2019 with 55.5%; post-election protests killed 8; Nusantara capital in East Kalimantan announced August 2019. Construction began 2022. All core facts confirmed.

title: Omnibus Job Creation Law — sweeping labor and investment deregulation
note: Passed 5 October 2020; Constitutional Court ruled it conditionally unconstitutional November 2021; revised version issued by presidential regulation December 2022. All core facts confirmed.

title: COVID-19 pandemic — first recession since 1998
note: First cases March 2020; economy contracted 2.07% in 2020 (first recession since 1998 Asian crisis). $48B stimulus confirmed. 700,000+ cases and 20,000 deaths by year-end are plausible given low testing. Core facts confirmed.

title: COVID-19 delta wave overwhelms hospitals — 500,000 estimated deaths
note: Delta variant devastated Indonesia mid-2021; daily deaths ~2,000 in July; oxygen shortages confirmed; excess mortality estimates exceeding 500,000 consistent with multiple studies. 400M+ doses administered confirmed.

title: G20 Bali summit — Indonesia's diplomatic peak
note: G20 summit held 15–16 November 2022 in Bali; joint declaration achieved despite Russia-Ukraine divisions; Retno Marsudi's diplomatic role confirmed; Jokowi visited Kyiv and Moscow before summit. All core facts confirmed.

title: Kanjuruhan stadium disaster — 135 killed
note: 1 October 2022; 135 killed; Arema FC match; police tear gas triggered crush. Several officers convicted. FIFA-mandated reforms followed. All core facts confirmed.

title: Prabowo wins presidential election — first-round victory
note: Prabowo won February 2024 election with 58.6% in first round; Gibran (Jokowi's son) as VP after Constitutional Court ruling on age limit. Human rights concerns noted by organisations. All core facts confirmed.

title: Prabowo government takes office — free meals program and coalition cabinet
note: Inaugurated 20 October 2024; large coalition cabinet; free nutritious meals program targeting schoolchildren confirmed as flagship policy with substantial budget. Nusantara capital challenges and fiscal criticism confirmed.

title: Papua conflict intensification — KKB attacks increase
note: TPNPB-OPM attacks intensified in 2025 including the April 2025 Yahukimo massacre (15 killed). HRW documented civilian casualties from military operations. Conflict remains largely invisible to international media. All core facts confirmed.
